# Separator

A line between groups.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Accessible first</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Accessible first:** Breaks between groups of questions.

- **Use it when:** Separating groups that spacing alone does not separate.
- **Not when:** Decoration between every item: spacing is quieter.

Instead:

- [Card](./card.md): A container, when groups need a boundary.

## How Accessible first uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Between page sections</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> space.gap.section</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A thin line</div></div><div class="cap">Space is easy to see; thin lines are not.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add separator
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Separator reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.

### Read straight from the system

Separator has no variables of its own yet; it reads these system tokens directly.
